rules.sentence: Hemangiomas greater than 4 cm, however, tend to cause abdominal pain and discomfort.
The most common symptoms are right upper quadrant pain, generalized abdominal pain, or abdominal fullness.
If bleeding occurs within the lesion, this can lead to expansion and inflammation of the capsule of Glisson and acute abdominal pain.
When the hemangioma becomes large, symptomatology is related to the compression of adjacent structures (ie, early satiety from gastric compression).
